newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma trooper who arrested McVeigh takes stand.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma trooper who arrested McVeigh takes stand.

text.p: Testimony in the Oklahoma City bombing trial resumed Monday with Oklahoma State Trooper Charles Hanger, who arrested Timothy McVeigh less than two hours after the April 1995 bombing, taking the stand.
The arrest took place north of Oklahoma City when Hanger saw McVeigh's yellow Mercury Marquis had a missing license plate. After stopping the car, Hanger noticed that McVeigh had a concealed weapon.

Hanger was the 10th witness to appear in the case against McVeigh, who is accused of murder and conspiracy in the April 19, 1995, bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City which killed 168 people.
The first nine witnesses were survivors, rescuers and victims' relatives who described in chilling detail the devastation caused by the attack.
McVeigh, who has pleaded not guilty, faces the death penalty if convicted.
